characters.name: Detective Sergeant Ronald "Ronnie" Brooks
characters.description: Beware the Nice Ones: He's mostly a friendly guy, but like Matt, he has a handful of moments where people realize that ticking him off is abadidea. Big Eater: Frequently seen snacking on various foods. It's even lampshaded by Natalie and Matt's constant teasing and when Alesha is savvy enough to bring him a pastry to bribe him into doing some research for her. Dead Partner: Andhow—his backstory includes a partner who was killed, Matt's the one who accidentally reminds him of this, eerilyForeshadowinghis own fate, andDI Wes Leyton (not his partner, but clearly a good enough friend for both of these tropes to apply) isgunned down on his birthdayat the beginning of the episode "Hard Stop". December–December Romance: In "Honor Bound", we learn that he had a relationship with a similarly aged fellow officer. Problem is, she was (and still is) married, and one of their trysts provides him with an alibi for a drug theft he's been implicated in. Disappeared Dad: Much like his US counterpart, he has a rocky relationship with both of his daughters thanks to his alcoholism and his two failed marriages (which are themselves due to his drinking problem).

characters.name: Detective Sergeant Matthew "Matt" Devlin
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: Ronnie calls Matt "Matty", "Matty-boy" or "Sunshine". Abusive Parents: Strongly implied—his contempt for a child abuser—"I know people like you", his feelings about victimized children in general, his empathy with an abused kid—"I've been that kid, Ronnie", and with a young woman who refers to her father as a "bastard"—"Are we related then, do you think?", but neither the extent nor specific perpetrator is ever made clear. Badass Adorable: He's gorgeous, amazingly polite... and in at least every other episode he runs down, disarms and disables a suspect, all while never cracking that well-mannered veneer. Beware the Nice Ones: He's a pretty nice guy... until/unless nasty abusers, rapists etc. tick him off.(As they interrogate a suspect)Matt:Come on, man. Don't make me play "bad cop".Ronnie:You wouldn't like him when he plays "bad cop". By-the-Book Cop: To the point where he once arrested a friend for using cocaine—right in front of him.

characters.name: Detective Sergeant Sam Casey
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: There's no explanation for his absence in Season 8. Contrasting Replacement Character: Despite some obvious similarities with his predecessor—young, good-looking, absent (and possibly abusive) father, there were some equally obvious differences—Matt's temper was generally limited to certain issues, whereas Sam appeared to have a short fuse abouteverything. Matt also clearly cherished the surrogate father he had in Ronnie. Sam seemed to resent Ronnie's attempts at being this—despite generally getting along, the two simply did not have the rapport that Matt and Ronnie did. Disappeared Dad: He had one and he is apparently unwillingly this to his own son, only getting to see him once a month. Heroic BSoD: Suffers an emotional shut-down throughout "Tracks", starting when he's unable to save a young victim of the train crash. Idiot Ball:Oh, Sam. You had to know that joking to a black suspect about what you have to do to get two weeks in Barbadoswould come back to bite you, right?No?Well how about sleeping with a perp posing as a "victim"? Not his smartest idea.

characters.name: Detective Sergeant Joe Hawkins
characters.description: But Not Too Black: He's mocked about his light skin by a dark-skinned suspect, who alternates between seeming jealous—insinuating that he's had an easier time because of it—or being contemptuous—calling him a "mongrel". He didn't take too kindly to it. Half-Breed Discrimination: As cited above, his reaction when a suspect calls him a "mongrel" indicates that this isn't the first time he's dealt with comments like this. Naïve Newcomer: Subverted. He's new to the Homicide Division, but he's been a detective for some time.

characters.name: Detective Inspector Natalie Chandler
characters.description: Iron Lady: Despite her obvious grief and anger, she waits until she's alone in her office with the blinds drawn to cry overMatt's death, and she refuses to break down despite the overwhelming evidence that her father is a killer. Mama Bear: Is fiercely defensive of her subordinates, takes it badly when someone is criticizing or harming them (e.g. Alesha's assault), and them screwing up provokes a reaction much like that of a disappointed/angry parent. Put on a Bus: Her absence in Season 7 is explained as her taking a leave of absence to care for her ill mother.She resurfaces in the 4th episode of Series 8, but technically not as a cop, but rather as the daughter of their prime suspect.

characters.name: Detective Inspector Wes Leyton
characters.description: Died on Their Birthday:He celebrates his birthday in theCold Openof the episode "Hard Stop"... and is shot and killed after leaving the party. Surprisingly Sudden Death:He's abruptly gunned down a few minutes into "Hard Stop". We Hardly Knew Ye: Appeared for only a series and a halfbefore his death.

characters.name: Senior Crown Prosecutor James Steel
characters.description: Chekhov's Skill: His previous experience as a defense attorney saves his bacon when he's charged with "perverting the course of justice". Determinator: His reluctance to give a case up or use any means necessary to win is legendary, and actually comes back to bite him in the ass in his last episode: he gets arrested for perverting the course of justice after some evidence that would have exonerated a murder suspect six years previously was found to have gone missing. The same episode says that his conviction rate isninety three percent. Office Romance: He has relationships with his female colleagues. And his final scene with Alesha (as well as his reaction to her rape) reveals that he has feelings for her as well, even though it never gets beyond attraction. Put on a Bus: Although acquitted of charges of perverting the course of justice, he still feels ultimately responsible for theMiscarriage of Justicethat occurred—an innocent man went to prison, while a guilty man went free and killed several more victims—and decides to resign from the CPS. Tranquil Fury: His matter-of-fact demeanor when he declares that he'd like to see Alesha's rapist "locked in a room with his victims" does little to hide the fact that he'd like to be included.

characters.name: Senior Crown Prosecutor Jacob Thorne
characters.description: The Casanova: He seems to have bedded or flirted with nearly half the female lawyers in London. Hello, Attorney!: He's an attractive lawyer.

characters.name: Junior Crown Prosecutor Alesha Philips
characters.description: Break the Cutie: She's adorable, but gets drawn through hell: raped by her doctor, loses her friend/mentor before they get a chance to explore their feelings for each other, and another friend is killed saving her life beforetheycan explore their feelings for each other. Unlike most examples of this trope, she appears to have come out of each tragedy stronger than before. Character Development: She starts out as aNaïve Newcomer, but grows more and more confident and competent as time goes on—by Series 2 she handles the questioning of several witnesses, by Series 5, prosecutes several cases on her own, and the final mention of her at the beginning of Series 7 is that she's been transferred to a senior position in another division. Composite Character: Of Paul Robinette (as they're both black), Claire Kincaid (an eager neophyte), and Elizabeth Olivet (the episode where she's raped is a remake of the one where Olivet is). Everyone's Baby Sister: As seen in the episode "Alesha", when everyone in the group is infuriated by what's happened to her and they promptly go all out to bring her rapist to justice. James can barely stand to watch the video of her rape, while Matt can't bring himself to watch it at all.Iron LadyDI Chandler:I'd like to cut off his dick with a rusty hacksaw and ram it down his throat!" Hello, Attorney!: She's a very attractive female lawyer.

characters.name: Junior Crown Prosecutor Kate Barker
characters.description: Contrasting Replacement Character:  Kate’s messy hair, upfront attitude, andOop Northaccent are a contrast to the polished and more softly-spoken Alesha. Idiot Ball: Chats with an opposing attorney about the tactics Jake is likely to use, then acts shocked when (a) the woman undermines their strategy by preparing her witness, and (b) Jake and Henry read her the riot act for what she's done. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: Their personalities are radically different, but she still falls into the "pretty young woman" slot that Alesha filled.

characters.name: Director George Castle
characters.description: Chekhov's Skill: Like James, was a defense attorney for a while. Despite nearly two decades having passed since then, he does an excellent, if ultimately unsuccessful job of representing an old friend on a manslaughter charge. Papa Wolf: Much like DI Chandler, is fiercely protective of his underlings, yet doesn't tolerate mistakes from them.

characters.name: Director Henry Sharpe
characters.description: Suspiciously Similar Substitute: For George Castle.
